LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 10.3.1 WORD CLASS: CONJUNCTIONS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.3: Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Class: Conjunctions
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Class: Conjunctions, part of Strand 10 in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why do we join sentences? 2. Which words do we use to join sentences?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify conjunctions correctly in oral and written texts for fluency in speech,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Class: Conjunctions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. engage in short dialogues featuring conjunctions for fluency in speech,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Class: Conjunctions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use conjunctions in a variety of contexts for effective oral and written communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Class: Conjunctions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. realise the importance of conjunctions in communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Class: Conjunctions in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify conjunctions correctly in oral and written texts for fluency in speech,

   Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Class: Conjunctions helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. engage in short dialogues featuring conjunctions for fluency in speech,

   Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Class: Conjunctions helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. use conjunctions in a variety of contexts for effective oral and written communication,

   Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Class: Conjunctions helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. realise the importance of conjunctions in communication.

   Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Class: Conjunctions helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use the conjunctions (and, but, or, yet, so, for, nor) to talk about topics related to the theme,

2. construct sentences using the conjunctions (and, but, or, yet, so, for, nor) and type them on a digital device,

3. listen to a short dialogue containing the conjunctions (and, but, or, yet, so, for, nor) and discuss their usage with peers,

4. answer and ask questions involving conjunctions correctly. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use the conjunctions (and, but, or, yet, so, for, nor) to talk about topics related to the theme,
2. construct sentences using the conjunctions (and, but, or, yet, so, for, nor) and type them on a digital device,
3. listen to a short dialogue containing the conjunctions (and, but, or, yet, so, for, nor) and discuss their usage with peers,
4. answer and ask questions involving conjunctions correctly. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 10.3.1 Word Class: Conjunctions together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This competence are realised as the learner engages in assigned activities

collaboratively.

• Digital Literacy: This is enhanced as the learner interacts with technology while typing their sentences on a digital

device.

Values:
• Responsibility: It is seen as the learner engages in assigned roles and duties in different activities while learning

conjunctions.

• Unity: This is achieved as the learner shares the available resources like the digital devices so that peers can as well type

their sentences on the device.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Personal Hygiene: This is promoted as the learner listens to short dialogues on sanitation and how to take care of oneself.

Link to other Learning Areas:

• The learner relates the knowledge on conjunctions to similar concepts taught in Kiswahili.

• The learner relates content learnt from the theme of hygiene and sanitation to what is learnt in Agriculture and Creative

Arts.

Main points to remember:

1. identify conjunctions correctly in oral and written texts for fluency in speech,
2. engage in short dialogues featuring conjunctions for fluency in speech,
3. use conjunctions in a variety of contexts for effective oral and written communication,
4. realise the importance of conjunctions in communication.

Remember the key question: Why do we join sentences? 2. Which words do we use to join sentences?
